name: abl2
question: Which single change to the fine-tuning data or training improves held-out (dev) performance without losing points in another error category?
baseline_recipe: round 54's recipe: basics 6 writes + 4 bug fixes per concept, compose 3 writes + 1 bug fix per exercise, contrast and novel examples, 200 replay rows, no skill families, no averaging; lr 1.5e-5, batch 4, rows of 1024 tokens, 72 steps
decision_rule: keep a change if its dev score beats base_s1 by more than the seed-to-seed difference (|base_s1 - base_s2|) and no error category loses 2 or more extra points; the benchmark is reported, never used to decide

arms.name: data_dedup
arms.changes: remove exact duplicates and second answer bodies for the same task text

arms.name: data_cap_repeats
arms.changes: at most 3 examples per distinct answer body; 3 instead of 6 writes per hand-written concept

arms.name: data_no_replay
arms.changes: drop the 200 replayed rows of old library-code instruction data

arms.name: ft_average
arms.changes: blend the trained weights 50/50 with the starting weights

arms.name: seq_512
arms.changes: rows of 512 tokens, batch 8: same tokens per step, half the unrelated packed context
